- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike after a recent dip, true price often lags and corrects downward — cap forecast peak at 1–2% below observed max.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.1), model often overestimates mean — adjust forecast mean down by 2–5% for next 10–15 days.  
- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., >0.2) after a downtrend, model often overshoots — reduce forecast by 3–7% in first 3–5 days of new trend.  
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in early days of a 30d window, true price often reverts to mean — apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast if sentiment is flat or mildly negative.  
- If sentiment is negative and model forecasts are rising, assume “sentiment reversal” — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0 units per day until sentiment stabilizes.
